verdict: REJECT — 6 blockers, 9 advisories. The artifact's measurement discipline is genuinely strong: every one of its 12 cited digests reproduced exactly (5 repo sources, 7 prototype baselines), the prototype pin re-verified clean at a62509d6…, the SRC-02 coverage enumeration walk passes 11/11, the D-008 declaration shape and the D-012 elements the dispatch enumerates (two-custody stableId, per-install universe, (ID, provenance) discriminator, metadata-only admission, reservation, scope precedence, alias window) are all carried in schema form, the canonicalization probe points are clean at all four named places, and vocabulary hygiene holds (QUALIFIED/DEMONSTRATED appear only in the two lawful negations; no duplicate keys in the subject's own bytes). But the finding-set delta is material: one DECIDED D-012 policy element (clause 6 in-class ownership transfer) is silently dropped and actively contradicted by RJ-1; the TC-NAME completeness claim is falsifiable and false (stale-alias missing); the commands block silently diverges from the pin in five measured fields with no DIFF entry — the exact failure class the artifact's own named-differences discipline exists to prevent; RJ-4 contradicts its own scope note; the mounted-root-command/name binding leaves a root-grammar collision admissible; and the corpus's own measured §7.5 duplicate-JSON-key attack class has no refusal code and no fixture class. Every blocker is repairable by bounded edits to this artifact; none requires reopening a source decision.

blockers.title: D-012 clause 6's DECIDED in-class ownership-transfer element is silently dropped, and RJ-1 as written contradicts it
blockers.detail: D-012 clause 6 (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at a3d0d266…, verified at bytes) decides two things for slice 1: transfer within the first-party/explicitly-trusted class 'is registry bookkeeping under host authority WITH the same two-custody update discipline', and the depth/third-party questions are deferred. The artifact carries the DEFERRED half twice (commands.parent note; whatThisDoesNotDo item 7) and the DECIDED half nowhere: no index-entry field, no transfer record shape, no status value, no prose clause names ownership transfer, and it is not listed as deferred. Worse than silence: transfer changes the provenance.publisher token for an unchanged stableId, and RJ-1's trigger ('stableId already has a live index entry with different provenance' → REFUSE_DUPLICATE_STABLE_ID) plus the retiredIds rule ('a different provenance claiming a retired ID is RJ-1') make the lawful post-transfer state a typed refusal with no carve-out for host-authorized in-class transfer. This is the silently-dropped-policy-element class the artifact's own reviewGuidance warns about (the D-012 lineage's twice-fallen trap). Repair: a transfer bookkeeping shape in indexSchema (or an explicit named deferral if the author believes clause 6's transfer cannot be schematized yet — but it is DECIDED, not deferred, so a schema carrier is owed), plus an RJ-1 exception clause scoped to host-authorized in-class transfer under the two-custody update discipline.

blockers.title: TC-NAME's warrant 'the full D-012 clause 7 negative-test enumeration, every member present' is false: stale-alias is absent; the clause's doctor-remediation requirement is not carried
blockers.detail: D-012 clause 7's enumeration (verified at bytes): 'collision, cycle, shadow, STALE-ALIAS, parent-linkage collision, reserved-name claim, the scope-precedence disclosure, ID/version distinctness, multi-version coexistence, AND a no-execution-during-admission probe'. TC-NAME carries nine items; stale-alias maps to none of them (the deprecation dual-clock data exists in indexSchema, but no fixture class exercises an alias past its window or the window transition). The warrant is a falsifiable universal claim and it fails by enumeration walk — the exact test the artifact invites. Additionally clause 7's closing sentence ('Namespace migrations require a recorded deprecation entry with typed doctor remediation') is half-carried: the deprecation entry exists, the typed doctor remediation has no binding point anywhere (the deprecation object carries no remediation ref, and ID-DEP-7 names DR-114 only for refusal-code/exit mapping, not for this). Repair: add the stale-alias fixture class to TC-NAME; add a doctor-remediation binding point (or reserved member) to the deprecation shape riding DR-114, named in identityDependencies.

blockers.title: Five measured prototype command-manifest fields diverge silently with no DIFF entry: output/rawStreamReason replaced by the differently-semantic outputModes; commonFlags, producesVerdict, producesEvidenceSnapshot, and manifest-level languages dropped
blockers.detail: PB-1's own measuredShape lists ToolCommandManifest's output, rawStreamReason, commonFlags, producesVerdict, producesEvidenceSnapshot and the manifest-level languages field (all verified present in manifest.ts at e0f47e6f…). The V2 commandSpecFields carry none of them and no DIFF names the divergence. These are not cosmetic: producesVerdict is how the prototype host knows an external command is suite-eligible WITHOUT importing the runtime (manifest.ts lines 137-143) — V2's schema loses that datum with no stated route; output/rawStreamReason (dispatch mode of the handler's return) is REPLACED by outputModes (host projection advertisement) — a semantic substitution, not a subset; languages is a CONSUMED prototype field (tools-list discovery, lines 238-244), not a reserved placeholder. DIFF-5 covers only the parse-closure narrowing. The dispatch standard and the artifact's own discipline ('eight NAMED differences') both make an unnamed schema-field divergence from the pin a finding — and here the artifact demonstrably measured the fields (they are in its PB-1 text) and then dropped them without a name. Repair: DIFF entries (or field carriers/reserved points) for each, with the outputModes substitution described as what it is. The requires→permissions narrowing, described inline at the permissions field but absent from the DIFF register, should be regularized in the same pass.

blockers.title: RJ-4 contradicts its own scope note: ENVELOPE_MISMATCH ('an envelope that does not verify over the canonicalized preimage') is not decidable without the ceremony or the open canonicalization; TC-SIG requires a fixture TC-BYTE-EXACT says cannot yet be required
blockers.detail: RJ-4's note claims the rule owns 'only the byte-level mismatch and absence classes, which are decidable without the ceremony'. UNSIGNED-presence and DIGEST_MISMATCH qualify (sha256 over stored bytes). ENVELOPE_MISMATCH does not: verifying an envelope over a canonicalized preimage requires (a) the canonical-JSON profile the artifact itself records as CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED with UR-1..5 open (ID-DEP-1, standing re-verified this review at 6f7c906c…), and (b) enough envelope-format/key semantics to run a verification — DR-112's surface. The same contradiction recurs in the corpus: TC-SIG requires an 'envelope-over-wrong-preimage mismatch' fixture, while TC-BYTE-EXACT's scopeNote rules that canonicalization vectors 'are required of THIS corpus only after that surface closes'. The signature-cell SPLIT itself is lawful (byte-level vs ceremony is a real boundary, honestly stated in whatThisDoesNotDo item 3) — the defect is that one subcode and one fixture class sit on the wrong side of it. Repair: move ENVELOPE_MISMATCH and the wrong-preimage fixture behind the ID-DEP-1/ID-DEP-5 conditionality (the D-002 symmetry-clause form the artifact already uses for TC-BYTE-EXACT), leaving RJ-4 with the genuinely ceremony-free classes.

blockers.title: The binding between manifest.name and the mounted root command's name is unstated, leaving a host-root-grammar collision admissible under RJ-2's literal collision universe
blockers.detail: The schemas record the mounted root command twice — commands[] (the one parent-less entry, with its own 'name') and indexSchema entries[].mountedRootCommand — while collision computation is defined over namesSnapshot ('the name + aliases the admission bound'). No rule requires commands[root].name == manifest.name, and RJ-2's trigger enumerates collisions 'over name, alias, or parent linkage against the reserved list, live names/aliases, or within the manifest's own command tree' — another component's mountedRootCommand is not in that universe. Hostile pair: component A (name 'aaa', root command 'zzz') admits; component B (name 'zzz') then admits under RJ-2 as written — 'zzz' is in no namesSnapshot — and the host root grammar double-mounts, the exact defect ADR-0159/PB-7 exists to refuse. Note the irony: DIFF-2's own reasoning ('the two-key shape only ever holds by assertion... collapsing the keys removes the invariant instead of guarding it') is un-applied to the name/root-command pair the collapse left behind. Repair: one line — either commands[root].name MUST equal manifest.name (making mountedRootCommand a pure custody echo), or mounted root command names enter the live-name collision universe and namesSnapshot explicitly includes them.

blockers.title: No duplicate-JSON-key refusal class and no duplicate-key fixture class, despite the corpus's own measured §7.5 attack lineage
blockers.detail: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §7.5 (measured sweep, 493 executions) records exactly this attack: json parsing without a pairs hook keeps the LAST duplicate key, 'so a document can say one thing to a reader and another to every instrument'. A manifest whose bytes carry {"stableId": A, ... "stableId": B} has ONE admission digest (sha256 of exact bytes — the encodingRule) yet presents DIFFERENT content to different parsers: the custody join (manifestDigest) verifies while the parsed identity, name set, tree entries, or declarations diverge between the admitting host and any later consumer. RJ-6's subcode list has no DUPLICATE_KEY member, the encodingRule says only 'a single JSON document', and grep over the subject finds zero duplicate-key coverage in any refusal or fixture class (TC-BYTE-EXACT, whose entire purpose is bytes-vs-parse fidelity, is the natural home). For an exact-byte admission cell this is the highest-value missing refusal in the artifact. Repair: an RJ-6 subcode (duplicate key anywhere in manifest/index/lock bytes is malformed) plus a TC-BYTE-EXACT fixture whose duplicate-key bytes are digest-pinned — noting such a fixture exists ONLY as pinned bytes, like the NFC classes.

advisories.title: PB-1 citation imprecision: the user-global sidecar is documented at manifest.ts lines 72-76 (ToolSource), not in the fileoverview lines 1-24 as cited
advisories.detail: The fileoverview names the sidecar only for project-local tools; the claim ('JSON sidecar for user-global/project-local') is substantively TRUE against the file but the cited line range supports only half of it.

advisories.title: TC-PATH has no '.'-segment fixture although RJ-3's trigger refuses '.' segments
advisories.detail: Eleven of the pathRule's refusal atoms have fixture classes; '.' does not. The twelve listed classes are otherwise real threats and fully cover the TM storage-namespace lineage's defeated-attack precedents (case-folding, Unicode normalization, traversal — verified against the freeze's TM row). Windows-only classes (reserved device names, trailing dot/space) are lawfully absent while Windows is deferred per D-002, but naming that deferral in TC-PATH would make the omission visible.

advisories.title: capabilities is required with no mayBeEmpty ruling; the artifact's own worked example cannot be translated under the schema as written
advisories.detail: dependencies and permissions carry explicit 'mayBeEmpty: true'; capabilities does not, and the cargo-clippy manifest (PB-2) declares NO capabilities. Whether its V2 translation admits with an empty array or refuses MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD is undecidable from the artifact. The internal-coherence walk otherwise passes: every other PB-2 datum (identity, aliases, parent-nested commands, requires→permissions, config→configuration, license→declarations, the user-installed clippy binary→the DR-119 prerequisites exception shape) has an unambiguous carrier.

advisories.title: The relation between entries[].status ('retired'/'revoked') and the retiredIds ledger is unspecified
advisories.detail: Is a retired component present in both records? Which does RJ-1 consult (its trigger names live entries and retiredIds, but 'live' is undefined against the four status values)? What are the readmission semantics of 'revoked' — same as retired, or DR-112-owned? One defining sentence closes this.

advisories.title: ID-DEP-4's consequence understates its own ride: lock RESOLUTION, not just admission, cannot evaluate versionConstraint until DR-111 closes
advisories.detail: The dependency is named (constraint language is DR-111's), so this is not an unnamed ride; but the consequence line covers only admission window-evaluation, while lockSchema.resolutionInputs.request and the closure rule both require constraint evaluation to produce any lock at all. State the consequence at its full width.

advisories.title: No stated caps: manifest size, tree entry count, path length, alias count
advisories.detail: The treeCommitmentShape alternatives note itself asks 'whether size bounds need a stated cap' — the honest self-flag deserves an answer or a named owner (DR-115's threshold machinery or DR-120's contract are candidates); unbounded manifests are a denial-of-service surface at metadata-only admission.

advisories.title: DIFF-2 slightly overstates the prototype drift guard
advisories.detail: manifest-assert.ts (PB-6, verified at bytes) holds id == identity.name and id == runtime name; the display 'name' field is NOT held equal to either. The measuredPrototypeBaselines PB-6 text states this correctly; DIFF-2's 'held equal... when they diverge' lumps the display name into the equality set.

advisories.title: Two host-owned vocabularies the refusals ride are not in identityDependencies: the permission token vocabulary (RJ-6/UNKNOWN_PERMISSION_TOKEN) and the configuration classification vocabulary
advisories.detail: Both are named inline (DR-105/DR-G09; SRC-03 host-owned classification) and in whatThisDoesNotDo, so this is mentioning-without-carrying rather than silence: the refusal subcodes are undecidable until some surface mints the vocabularies, and no ID-DEP row names which. A tenth and eleventh dependency row (or folding into ID-DEP-7's pattern) regularizes it.

advisories.title: PB-5's enforced-by parenthetical merges ADR-0159's enforced-by list with its enforcement-reason mechanism
advisories.detail: The ADR's yaml enforced-by names suites-reserved-names.test.ts and reserved-names.test.ts; reject-host-command-collisions.ts is named in the enforcement-reason as the admission gate. The artifact's '(enforced-by: reserved-names.test.ts, reject-host-command-collisions.ts)' is substantively right and citationally blended.
